facts.raw_span: a red tumor on her right upper arm that enlarged over 6 months
The lesion initially started as a small cutaneous nodule
no history of local trauma or insect bite
a 6 × 6-cm protuberant, thick-walled, and well-defined red bullalike tumor on the right upper arm
a nontender, firm-to-hard nodule was palpated
no regional lymphadenopathy
Hematologic, biochemical, and urinalysis tests were normal
multilocular spaces below the epidermis and a solid tumor present in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance
basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis and dilated lymphatic vessels in the dermis above the tumor

concepts.why: The presence of a red tumor with a hard nodule, multilocular spaces, and basophilic cells with shadow cells is consistent with pilomatrixoma, a type of benign skin tumor.

The rapid growth and appearance of the tumor, along with its location on the arm, could suggest keratoacanthoma, although the lack of typical crater-like appearance and the presence of shadow cells make it less likely.
The firm-to-hard nodule and the tumor's appearance could be consistent with dermatofibroma, but the presence of multilocular spaces and shadow cells is not typical for this condition.
